prompt: jq |= update-assignment RHS produces no values
answer:
For `|=`, if the RHS produces no values (`empty`), jq deletes the path being updated:

```jq
{a: 1} | .a |= empty
```

produces:

```jq
{}
```

This differs from ordinary assignment:

```jq
{a: 1} | .a = empty
```

which produces no output at all. The jq wiki documents this distinction: `.a = empty` yields an empty stream, while `.a |= empty` leaves `null` unchanged or deletes the targeted path.

For multiple paths, behavior—especially in jq 1.6—can be buggy or inconsistent. For example:

```jq
[1, 2] | .[] |= empty
```

may produce:

```jq
[2]
```

rather than deleting every element. Use `del()` when deletion is intended:

```jq
[1, 2] | del(.[])
```

produces:

```jq
[]
```

The jq language description states that the intended current `_modify` behavior is: only the first RHS value is used, and if the RHS produces no values, the path is deleted. (Search results: [jq wiki](https://github-wiki-see.page/m/jqlang/jq/wiki/jq-Language-Description), [jq pitfalls](https://github-wiki-see.page/m/jqlang/jq/wiki/How-to%3A-Avoid-Pitfalls), [issue #2397](https://github.com/stedolan/jq/issues/2397).)
